notes: Correct, simple classification that treats non-literal names as dynamic, as the reference does, but it re-parses every expression on every upstream response with no caching, and it duplicates the expansion regexes.

The classification is functionally correct and focused, but it re-runs regex expansion and a full CEL parse for every matcher set on every proxied response, a needless hot-path cost; it also duplicates the regexes.

The AST classification is sound, but response matchers are only computed in Handler.Provision, so handlers built without Provision (as the existing and hidden tests do) never retry on responses, and the package suite fails.

This is a clean provision-time selection of response matcher sets that handles .ph, dynamic names and lookalikes. It depends on Handler.Provision, which unit tests bypass, so the hidden response-retry tests and the suite fail; the regex expansion is duplicated.

Functionally right, but the hot path always calls the CEL-parsing check before consulting the cache, so the cache is useless and every response is re-parsed; it also adds unnecessary rp.* and value-type handling.

It parses the expanded expression's ph() calls with exact and prefix name matching and conservative handling of dynamic names, precomputes the result at provision, and falls back to computing it per request when unprovisioned. It duplicates the placeholder regexes and adds unneeded rp./value-type handling.

Sharing the expansion logic through internal.ExpandCELPlaceholders is cleaner, but like C2 it depends entirely on Provision-time state and breaks response retries for unprovisioned handlers, so the hidden suite fails.

It shares placeholder expansion via the top-level internal package and the AST analysis is correct, but it relies on Handler.Provision to fill responseRetryMatch, so unit-built handlers lose response retries and the suite fails. Its tests cover only negative cases.

Has the most thorough edge-case handling and tests (e.g. .ph, cel.bind, transport-error retries), but it adds a new internal package, a celmatcher refactor and an integration test, and its Provision-only cache breaks response retries under the hidden test harness.

The detection logic is sound and the expansion code is shared, and it works in production. However, response-retry selection only gets populated in Handler.Provision, so unit-built handlers (including the hidden tests' helper) never do response retries and the suite fails; it also adds a new internal package, a celmatcher refactor and an integration test.

Parses the expanded expression to find response placeholders and caches the result at Provision, with a runtime fallback for unprovisioned handlers; it duplicates the placeholder-expansion regexes from celmatcher instead of reusing the provisioned AST.

It is correct with a provision-time cache, a per-request fallback, and static evaluation of concatenated names. It duplicates the regexes, has an odd linter-appeasing switch, and accidentally truncates brokenUpstreamAddr's doc comment.
